records.title: AI authorization EU-101 (fictional)
records.text: On 2026-09-02, the claims operations director, Marta Lindqvist, authorized the claims triage assistant to sort incoming warranty claims into priority queues. The system is classified as not high-risk under the AI Act, because it does not decide outcomes for individuals. It is used in line with the provider's instructions for use, version 4. Two claims supervisors, both trained on the assistant, oversee its queues each day and can switch it off at any time. System logs are kept for twelve months.

sources.title: Risk classification memo RC-101
sources.text: The claims triage assistant is not high-risk under the AI Act; it orders a queue and makes no decision about any individual.

records.title: AI authorization EU-104 (fictional)
records.text: On 2026-11-03, the HR director authorized the shift-planning assistant to propose weekly rotas for warehouse staff. It is classified as high-risk under Annex III because it allocates work. Warehouse employees and their works council were informed before it went live. The duty manager reviews every proposed rota and may reject it. Logs are kept for at least six months.

records.title: AI authorization EU-106 (fictional)
records.text: On 2026-09-30, the benefits office manager authorized the eligibility assistant to recommend whether applicants qualify for a housing grant. The system is high-risk under Annex III. Applicants are told in their decision letter that an AI system assisted the assessment. A caseworker trained on the system checks each recommendation and can override it. The office follows the provider's instructions for use and reports any serious incident to the provider. Logs are kept for two years.
